title: First-Principles Investigation of the {ScSe2} TMDs Monolayer: Structural Stability, Electronic and Optical Properties
abstract: We present an ab initio investigation of the {ScSe2} monolayer using density functional theory (DFT), as employed in the CP2K code, to assess its structural stability and electronic properties. The electronic behavior of both phases is governed by the local coordination environment of scandium and the associated lifting of degeneracy of its $3d$ orbitals. The valence bands (VBs) are dominated by {Se}$-4p$ states in both phases, while the states near the Fermi level distinguish the metallic 1T phase from the semiconducting 2H phase. Optical response calculations reveal markedly different spectral signatures for the two polymorphs. Two findings emerge from this study: a polymorphism-driven metal-to-semiconductor transition without any change in chemical composition and distinct optical responses relevant to phase-selective optoelectronic devices.

summaries.en: First-principles DFT calculations show that the ScSe2 monolayer's structural stability, electronic properties, and optical response are governed by scandium's local coordination and 3d orbital splitting, producing a polymorphism-driven metal-to-semiconductor transition from the metallic 1T phase to the semiconducting 2H phase with distinct phase-selective optical signatures.

title: Wireless readout and control of cavity magnon-polaritons via photonic modes delocalised across a gap
abstract: In cavity magnonics, photon-magnon hybridisation is typically detected by measuring the cavity response (i.e. measuring cavity resonance shifts through its reflection or transmission spectra). While a large body of work in the field has focused on three-dimensional cavities, a variety of two-dimensional resonators have also been explored as hosts for photonic modes due to their compatibility with on-chip integration. Nevertheless, the readout approach remains largely unchanged. Here, we demonstrate remote excitation and readout of cavity magnon-polaritons using two spatially separated, wirelessly coupled ring resonators. Through inductive coupling, energy is transferred between the resonators, enabling the magnonic system to be excited by one resonator while its hybrid-mode spectrum is detected through measurements of the other. We demonstrate wireless readout of cavity magnon-polaritons at separations ranging from millimetres to centimetres, identifying their characteristic response in the remotely measured spectrum. This establishes wireless resonator coupling as a route to remote interrogation of hybrid photon-magnon systems.

summaries.en: The paper demonstrates wireless excitation and readout of cavity magnon-polaritons using two spatially separated, inductively coupled ring resonators, where one resonator excites the magnonic system and the other remotely detects its hybrid-mode spectrum across gaps from millimetres to centimetres.

title: A High-Frequency Flux-Driven DC-SQUID Threshold Detector at the Single-Microwave-Photon Energy Scale: A Numerical Feasibility Study
abstract: In our recent work (Phys. Rev. B \textbf{113}, 224503 (2026)), we showed numerically that rapidly sweeping the bias current of a current-biased Josephson junction threshold detector (CBJJ-JTD) drives it out of equilibrium. This substantially reduces the effect of thermal noise on microwave detection and may enable threshold detection near the energy of a single microwave photon. The scheme requires very low damping ($\beta \leq 10^{-4}$) and a very fast bias-current sweep ($v/\beta \geq 1$), both of which are difficult to achieve with available junctions and low-pass-filtered cryogenic measurement lines. Here we propose a more experimentally accessible nonequilibrium threshold detector based on a high-frequency flux-driven direct-current superconducting quantum interference device (DC-SQUID) and investigate it by numerically solving the resistively and capacitively shunted junction (RCSJ) equations. The applied flux drives a circulating supercurrent and sustains nonequilibrium phase dynamics throughout the bias-current sweep, removing the need for a fast sweep or for transient oscillations set by the initial phase. Using typical experimental device parameters, we calculate switching-current distributions (SCDs) with and without a microwave input for both driven and undriven SQUIDs. We quantify detection performance using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and their area under the curve (AUC). The simulations show that high-frequency flux drive reduces the impact of thermal noise and enables statistical discrimination of weak microwave pulses at the single-photon energy scale. We also numerically estimate detector characteristics such as phase selectivity and dynamic range.

summaries.en: A numerical RCSJ study shows that a high-frequency flux-driven DC-SQUID threshold detector can suppress thermal-noise effects and statistically discriminate weak microwave pulses at the single-microwave-photon energy scale, offering a more experimentally accessible alternative to fast-swept current-biased Josephson junction detectors.

title: Thickness-Dependent Morphology and Electrical Transport in Ultrathin Amorphous MoSi Films
abstract: We investigate the thickness-dependent surface morphology and electrical transport of ultrathin amorphous Mo50Si50 films deposited by magnetron co-sputtering. Atomic force microscopy of Si-capped heterostructures on Si/SiO2 reveals smooth surfaces throughout the investigated thickness range, with RMS roughness below 0.2 nm and a non-monotonic thickness dependence characterized by a minimum at 1.92 nm. Room-temperature sheet resistance follows an approximately inverse-thickness dependence for films with nominal thicknesses of about 1.9-5 nm, whereas a pronounced deviation from this scaling develops below approximately 1.5-2 nm. Temperature-dependent measurements further reveal a superconducting transition in the 30-nm film, while the 1.54-nm film shows a strong resistance increase upon cooling clearly indicates a superconductor-insulator transition. In the 2-20 K range, the sheet conductance of the 1.54-nm film exhibits a reproducible logarithmic temperature dependence, Gs(T)=G0+Bln(T/T0), consistent with quantum corrections to diffusive transport in a strongly disordered quasi-two-dimensional conductor. These results identify a thickness-sensitive transport regime in ultrathin MoSi while demonstrating that the corresponding heterostructures retain comparatively smooth surface morphology.

title: Tuning of superconducting and physical properties of Mo$_{1-x}$Si$_x$ thin films for Superconducting Nanowire Single-Photon Detector Applications
abstract: We investigate the normal-state electrical properties of ultrathin amorphous Mo$_{1-x}$Si$_x$ films deposited by DC magnetron co-sputtering over a broad range of compositions and thicknesses. Films with Si contents of $x = 0.14$ to $0.5$ were deposited on Si/SiO$_2$ and Si/Si$_3$N$_4$ substrates (monocrystalline Si with SiO$_2$ and S$_3$N$_4$ buffer layers respectfully); X-ray diffraction confirms an amorphous structure across the full composition range, while X-ray reflectometry is used to verify film thicknesses. The room-temperature sheet resistance ranges from 110 to 1990 $\Omega/\square$, corresponding to resistivities of 125-478 $\mu\Omega\cdot$cm. The sheet resistance generally increases with increasing Si content and decreasing film thickness, although the coupled variation of composition and thickness limits the quantitative separation of these effects. Additional measurements on thicker reference films show superconducting transition temperatures between 5.2 and 7.7 K, with $T_c$ decreasing monotonically at higher Si contents. A comparison of films on different substrate types shows no systematic difference between Si/SiO$_2$ and Si/Si$_3$N$_4$, while films on Al$_2$O$_3$ exhibit elevated sheet resistance at the lower thicknesses. These results characterize the accessible parameter space of our deposition process and provide a basis for the selection of film stoichiometry for detector fabrication.

title: Observation of nonadiabatic quantum tunneling in a driven correlated insulator
abstract: Many emerging solid-state platforms for Floquet engineering, nonlinear transport, and high harmonic generation operate near the Keldysh crossover, where optical fields are sufficiently strong and fast to reshape electronic states on sub-cycle timescales. Despite its importance, the microscopic pathways for photocarrier generation in this regime remain poorly understood, as neither perturbative multiphoton absorption nor adiabatic tunneling provides an adequate description. Here, we perform time-resolved optical spectroscopy on the correlated van der Waals insulator NiPS$_3$ while systematically tuning the drive electric field and frequency over a wide range. In the crossover regime, we observe multiphoton-like resonances that are blue-shifted by ponderomotive effects within an otherwise tunneling-dominated absorption channel - a clear spectroscopic signature of adiabaticity breakdown. Hubbard-model simulations based on a time-dependent Gaussian variational approach qualitatively reproduce these features. Together, our results elucidate the microscopic mechanisms of charge excitation in the Keldysh crossover regime and identify a key ingredient for controlling strong-field nonlinear dynamics in correlated materials.

summaries.en: Time-resolved optical spectroscopy of the correlated van der Waals insulator NiPS3 across a wide range of drive fields and frequencies reveals multiphoton-like resonances blue-shifted by ponderomotive effects within a tunneling-dominated absorption channel, providing a spectroscopic signature of adiabaticity breakdown in the Keldysh crossover regime that is qualitatively reproduced by time-dependent Gaussian variational Hubbard-model simulations.

title: A Fiber-Optic Platform for Cryogenic Laser-Pump Neutron-Probe Magneto-Optical Measurements
abstract: We report a fiber-optic laser-pump neutron-probe method for momentum- and frequency-resolved magneto-optical measurements. The technique uses inelastic neutron scattering to measure time-dependent two-point magnetization correlations, S(Q,$\omega$), after resonant photoexcitation at cryogenic temperatures. We demonstrate it by measuring nonequilibrium thermalization dynamics in Yb-based quantum magnets.

summaries.en: The paper reports a fiber-optic laser-pump neutron-probe technique that uses inelastic neutron scattering to measure time-dependent two-point magnetization correlations S(Q,ω) after resonant photoexcitation at cryogenic temperatures, demonstrated on nonequilibrium thermalization dynamics in Yb-based quantum magnets.

title: Ballistic propagation-mediated super-resolution light-element imaging: in-situ tracking dynamic hydrogen migration
abstract: Transmission electrons - with few-picometer wavelengths - can theoretically resolve all atoms in solids. However, constrained by factors such as lens aberrations, Z-contrast dependence and poor temporal resolution, the scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) fails to tackle the long-standing challenge of hydrogen dynamics on atomic scale. Here, our experiment-guided simulations reveal that unlike heavy-atom imaging - governed by wave-based imaging process - ballistic propagation of particle-like electrons in Cs-corrected TEM enables super-resolution imaging (SRI) of light atoms, achieving a resolution down to 14 pm and a robust hydrogen contrast of ~24%. Our in-situ SRI study not only uncovers polymetric hydrogen aggregation in TiHx and H-LaAlO3, but also inter-site migration, rotational displacement of hydrogen species and collective hydrogen tunneling-induced polarization surge in the oxide. By exploiting the novel electron-matter interactions, our findings offer an unparalleled approach to probe hydrogen dynamics and establish accurate structure-property relationships in diverse functional materials.
subjects: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci) ; Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph); Instrumentation and Detectors (physics.ins-det)

summaries.en: Experiment-guided simulations show that ballistic propagation of particle-like electrons in Cs-corrected TEM enables super-resolution imaging of light atoms with 14 pm resolution and ~24% hydrogen contrast, allowing in-situ tracking of hydrogen aggregation and migration dynamics in TiHx and H-LaAlO3.

title: Inferring Experimental Objectives in Microscopy Experiments from Decision Traces
abstract: Modern microscopes can acquire, analyze and act on data far faster than human operators can decide what to measure next. Exploiting this speed in automated experiments requires the instrument to follow the scientific logic of the operator, and one way to encode that logic is through reward functions that become part of the operation process. Here we explore whether such reward functions can be learned from the decision histories of microscope operators. We propose multiple frameworks in which recorded choices among alternative measurement locations serve as comparative evidence about the operator's preferences, and we compare several algorithms for reconstructing the reward including interpretable linear models built on physically meaningful image descriptors, nonlinear functions of the same descriptors, an unsupervised image representation followed by preference modeling, and a preference trained deep kernel inspired model. The result of this analysis is a spatial field of reward functions over the sample that can be used to run the instrument. We also propose a way to benchmark these approaches, based on withheld decisions and on decision histories generated with known objectives. We then examine the possibility that a decision history contains changing priorities throughout the experiment. A hidden Markov model assigns distinct rewards to recurring selection strategies, whereas a continuous-state model tracks smoothly varying preference weights. Controlled sequences generated over real microscopy candidate sets show that both concealed switches and gradual drift can be recovered. These reward functions, learned directly from recorded decisions, provide candidate objectives for future automated microscopy experiments.

summaries.en: This paper explores learning reward functions that encode microscope operators' scientific logic from their recorded decision histories among measurement locations, comparing interpretable linear models, nonlinear models, unsupervised image representations, and deep kernel methods, and showing via hidden Markov and continuous-state models that both concealed priority switches and gradual preference drift can be recovered from controlled decision sequences on real microscopy candidate sets.

title: Indentation-induced polar domain reconfiguration in the charge-density-wave semiconductor EuTe4
abstract: Controlling polar domains in conducting materials by external fields could unlock polarization-based electronic functionalities, yet remains experimentally challenging. While mechanical actuation driven by local strain, stress, or strain gradients has been proposed as an external-voltage-free route, its experimental demonstration in relatively conducting polar materials remains limited. Here we demonstrate mechanically induced polar-domain reconfiguration in the charge-density-wave (CDW) semiconductor EuTe4 at room temperature, whose resistivity is on the order of 10 m$\Omega$cm. Polarized-light microscopy and second-harmonic-generation measurements reveal CDW-induced in-plane polarization domains with an approximately 90 $^\circ$ domain configuration. Local indentation with a $\sim$1 $\mu$m-apex-radius needle reconfigures these domains, producing write/erase-like changes in wedge-shaped regions. These results establish local mechanical-field domain engineering in a relatively conducting CDW semiconductor, with possible contributions from both ferroelastic-like and flexoelectric mechanisms.

summaries.en: Local indentation with a ~1 µm-apex-radius needle mechanically reconfigures CDW-induced in-plane polarization domains in the relatively conducting charge-density-wave semiconductor EuTe4 at room temperature, as revealed by polarized-light microscopy and second-harmonic-generation measurements.

title: Anatomy of orbital and spin responses in GaAs and Si: Hall, inverse Faraday, and magneto-optical Kerr effects
abstract: Magneto-optical signals in nonmagnetic semiconductors entangle spin and orbital contributions, both in angular-momentum generation and magneto-optical detection. We calculate these contributions for electron-doped GaAs and Si using density-functional theory, linear-response theory, and a second-order density-matrix treatment of the inverse Faraday effect. At small electron doping, the intrinsic orbital Hall conductivity exceeds its spin counterpart in magnitude, while the orbital contribution to light-induced magnetization dominates over broad photon-energy ranges. We show that orbital- and spin-resolved optical Hall and polar Kerr coefficients exhibit stronger sensitivity to orbital moments than to equal spin moments. This contrast reflects direct electric-dipole coupling to orbital motion versus spin-orbit-mediated coupling to spin polarization. Consequently, Si maintains a substantial orbital magneto-optical response despite its weak spin-orbit interaction. At probe energies of 1.5 eV in GaAs and 3.0 eV in Si, the magnitude of the Kerr rotation per unit orbital moment is approximately 5 and 13 times larger than that per unit spin moment, respectively. Combining the calculated Hall conductivities and Kerr coefficients with a phenomenological drift-diffusion model yields predominantly orbital edge signals for the assumed diffusion constants and relaxation lengths. These results indicate that optical detection of induced magnetization in doped semiconductors such as GaAs and Si can be dominated by orbital signals, and therefore cannot be interpreted solely in terms of spin polarization.

title: Critical Topology: A New Perspective for Phase Transitions
abstract: Critical topology has emerged as a form of quantum criticality beyond the Landau paradigm, challenging conventional approaches to classifying universality classes by introducing topological properties as an additional criterion. Despite substantial progress over the past five years, several fundamental questions remain open. Theoretically, can we establish a general criterion for the emergence of critical topology? Can a unified theoretical framework be extended beyond one-dimensional quantum many-body systems? What efficient numerical methods can be developed to investigate critical topological states in higher-dimensional strongly correlated systems? Experimentally, research has so far focused primarily on single-particle critical topology. An important next step is to realize and characterize many-body critical topology in quantum systems using platforms such as Rydberg atom arrays, superconducting quantum processors, and quantum materials. Major advances in statistical physics often arise from re-examining fundamental concepts. The theory of critical phenomena developed by Landau, Ginzburg, and Wilson, together with the topological phase transitions pioneered by Kosterlitz and Thouless, has now inspired new discoveries in artificial acoustic metamaterials. These experimental observations mark a beginning rather than an endpoint for research on critical topology, and further advances in this direction are anticipated.

summaries.en: This paper reviews critical topology as a form of quantum criticality beyond the Landau paradigm, outlining open theoretical questions about general criteria, higher-dimensional and unified frameworks, and efficient numerical methods, and calling for experimental realization of many-body critical topology in platforms such as Rydberg atom arrays, superconducting quantum processors, and quantum materials.

title: Scanning nanowire quantum dot with radio-frequency read-out
abstract: Scanning single-electron transistors (SETs) are highly sensitive local probes of charge and electric potential, but their integration with robust height control for scanning probe microscopy remains challenging. Furthermore, readout bandwidths are limited to tens of kHz, while characterizing faster charge dynamics is often of interest. Here, we present a scanning SET in the form of a nanowire (NW) quantum dot (QD) integrated at the apex of a non-contact atomic force microscopy (NC-AFM) cantilever. We demonstrate NC-AFM topographic imaging and local electrometry capability by mapping the electrostatic potential generated by a set of nanoscale voltage-biased gate electrodes. Comparison with electrostatic simulations shows agreement with the measured potential profiles. We demonstrate radio-frequency (rf) reflectometry read-out of the sensor, by embedding the QD in an LC-resonator. This platform establishes a route towards high-bandwidth scanning electrometry with simultaneous topographic contrast.

summaries.en: The paper presents a scanning single-electron transistor based on a nanowire quantum dot integrated at the apex of a non-contact atomic force microscopy cantilever, enabling topographic imaging and local electrometry with radio-frequency reflectometry read-out via an LC resonator.
summaries.zh: 本文提出了一种扫描单电子晶体管，其形式为集成在非接触原子力显微镜悬臂尖端的纳米线量子点，可实现形貌成像和局部静电测量，并通过嵌入LC谐振器实现射频反射测量读出。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、非接触原子間力顕微鏡カンチレバーの先端に集積したナノワイヤ量子ドットを用いた走査型単一電子トランジスタを提示し、形状イメージングと局所静電測定を実現するとともに、LC共振器への埋め込みによる高周波反射測定読み出しを示す。

title: Femtosecond laser-controlled production of functional titanium niobate layers from TiO$_{2}$/Nb$_{2}$O$_{5}$ powders
abstract: Conventional synthesis methods of titanium niobates (TNO) require prolongated high-temperature treatments. To overcome this limitation, in this work, we have developed a confined powder-bed femtosecond (fs) laser-based technique to sinter TNO films starting from a mixture of TiO$_{2}$ and Nb$_{2}$O$_{5}$ powders, avoiding furnace-based approaches. The influence of laser-processing conditions on film formation, phase composition, and microstructure is systematically investigated, demonstrating that different TNO phases and morphologies can be obtained by controlling the laser pulse energy. A comprehensive characterization of the processed films has been performed, providing insights into the mechanisms governing their formation, which appear to share key features with laser-induced backward transfer (LIBT) processes. Our findings establish the relationship between laser-processing conditions and TNO film formation, highlighting the potential of confined powder-bed fs-laser processing as an alternative route for manufacturing functional oxide layers. Tentative applications of these layers are finally discussed.

summaries.en: A confined powder-bed femtosecond laser technique sinters functional titanium niobate films directly from TiO2/Nb2O5 powder mixtures without furnace treatment, with laser pulse energy controlling the resulting phases and morphologies.
summaries.zh: 一种限域粉床飞秒激光技术可直接从TiO2/Nb2O5混合粉末烧结出功能性铌酸钛薄膜而无需炉内处理，激光脉冲能量可调控所得物相与形貌。
summaries.ja: 閉じ込め粉末床フェムト秒レーザー技術により、TiO2/Nb2O5混合粉末から炉処理なしで機能性チタン酸ニオブ膜を直接焼結でき、レーザーパルスエネルギーによって生成相と形態を制御できる。

title: Two-dimensional Thyristor
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors offer a viable platform for next-generation electronics beyond sub-3 nm nodes, yet essential nonlinear circuit elements, such as thyristors, remain unexplored on atomically thin platforms. Here, we report an atomically thin reconfigurable electro-optical thyristor based on a lateral WSe2-MoSe2-WSe2-MoSe2 PNPN heterostructure, directly grown via sequential edge epitaxy. Unlike single-junction 2D diodes, this multijunction architecture exhibits thyristor-like nonlinear switching, including forward blocking, abrupt snapback, bistability, and electrical latching. The device exhibits a forward-blocking voltage of 183 V, corresponding to a critical electric field of 1 MV/cm. Under open-gate conditions, avalanche-assisted carrier multiplication and regenerative feedback are associated with a sharp forward-voltage drop of 175 V, a pronounced current surge, and an ultralow holding voltage. Gate-pulse modulation and temperature-dependent measurements indicate avalanche-assisted thyristor operation and latching behavior. This 2D lateral heterostructure enables a new route to nonlinear and bistable switching, latching, ultralow standby power, and adaptive logic, opening the way for reconfigurable 2D electronics and photonic integrated circuits.
subjects: Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall) ; Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

summaries.en: Researchers demonstrate an atomically thin lateral WSe2-MoSe2-WSe2-MoSe2 PNPN heterostructure thyristor grown by sequential edge epitaxy that exhibits nonlinear switching with a 183 V forward-blocking voltage (1 MV/cm critical field), abrupt 175 V snapback, bistability, and electrical latching arising from avalanche-assisted carrier multiplication and regenerative feedback.
summaries.zh: 研究人员展示了通过顺序边缘外延生长的原子级薄横向WSe2-MoSe2-WSe2-MoSe2 PNPN异质结构晶闸管，其具有183 V正向阻断电压（对应1 MV/cm临界电场）、175 V突变回跳、双稳态和电学锁存等非线性开关特性，这些特性源于雪崩辅助的载流子倍增与再生反馈。
summaries.ja: 研究者らは、逐次エッジエピタキシーで成長させた原子層厚の横型WSe2-MoSe2-WSe2-MoSe2 PNPNヘテロ構造サイリスタを報告し、183 Vの順方向阻止電圧（臨界電界1 MV/cm）、175 Vの急峻なスナップバック、双安定性、電気的ラッチングといった非線形スイッチング特性が、なだれ支援キャリア増倍と再生帰還に由来することを示した。

title: Gallium at germanium surfaces: links to superconducting films and correlated adatom lattices
abstract: Epitaxial films grown on Ge(001) show that germanium hyperdoped with substitutional Ga is superconducting. In earlier implanted films, Ga-rich precipitates obscured the origin of the superconductivity. This review examines the sites Ga occupies on Ge(001) and Ge(111) and how it enters the growing film. The Ga fraction expected from the growth fluxes is 17.9\%, yet the distribution of Ga among lattice sites is unknown. Comparisons include Ga on Si(001) and Si(111),In, Sn, Pb, Sb and P on Ge(001), and elemental and two-dimensional Ga. Where its surface coordination has been established, Ga has three bonds, whereas substitutional Ga in the films is fourfold coordinated and acts as an acceptor. Scanning tunnelling microscopy and X-ray standing waves have assigned Ga sites on Ge(111), but the dilute Ga site on Ge(001), where the films are grown, has yet to be measured. On Ge(111), Ga in the substrate may supply holes to the correlated Sn adatom lattice, as B supplies holes to the superconducting Sn lattice on Si(111). Whether Ga can supply holes depends on where it sits and whether it has three or four neighbours. On both surfaces, element-specific measurements and calculations comparing adsorption with substitution could settle the remaining site assignments.

summaries.en: This review examines the surface sites and incorporation pathways of Ga on Ge(001) and Ge(111) in relation to superconducting Ga-hyperdoped Ge films and correlated adatom lattices, highlighting that key dilute Ga site assignments remain unresolved.
summaries.zh: 本文综述了Ga在Ge(001)和Ge(111)表面的占位与掺入途径，及其与超导Ga超掺杂Ge薄膜和关联吸附原子晶格的关联，并指出关键的稀Ga占位归属仍未确定。
summaries.ja: 本レビューは、超伝導Ga過剰ドープGe薄膜および相関吸着原子格子との関連において、Ge(001)とGe(111)表面上のGaの占有サイトと取り込み経路を検討し、希薄Gaの主要なサイト帰属が未解決であることを指摘する。

title: Altermagnetism of MnSiN2 and MnGeN2 in a wurtzite-based crystal structure
abstract: Based on symmetry analysis, the Pna2_1 wurtzite-based crystal structure with Mn as a magnetic group-II element, MnSiN2 and MnGeN2 belong to the class of altermagnets because spin-up and spin-down Mn in the unit cell are related by rotation or mirror plane type operations rather than inversion or translation. Spin polarized density functional theory calculations and quasiparticle self-consistent (QS) GW calculations support the symmetry analysis and identify the lowest-energy spin configuration as Pna'2_1' in agreement with neutron diffraction data. The altermagnetic band splittings allowed for the three different antiferromagnetic ordering patterns are reported and symmetry analyzed. Additionally, spin wave dispersions, chiral magnon spltting, and Neel temperature estimates from the mean-field and random-phase approximations are provided, as well as calculations of the optical dielectric function using the Bethe-Salpeter Equation method. MnSiN2 exhibits both Wannier-type excitons with N-p to Si-s transition character and charge-transfer Frenkel-type excitons with hole on N-p and electron on Mn-d orbital character.

summaries.en: Symmetry analysis and spin-polarized DFT plus quasiparticle self-consistent GW calculations show that wurtzite-based MnSiN2 and MnGeN2 are altermagnets, with the lowest-energy Pna'2_1' spin configuration confirmed against neutron diffraction, and report their altermagnetic band splittings, spin-wave and chiral magnon properties, Neel temperature estimates, and Bethe-Salpeter optical dielectric functions exhibiting both Wannier-type and charge-transfer Frenkel-type excitons in MnSiN2.
summaries.zh: 对称性分析以及自旋极化密度泛函理论和准粒子自洽GW计算表明，基于纤锌矿结构的MnSiN2和MnGeN2属于交错磁体，其最低能自旋构型Pna'2_1'与中子衍射数据一致，并报道了其交错磁能带劈裂、自旋波与手性磁振子特性、奈尔温度估计以及Bethe-Salpeter光学介电函数，其中MnSiN2表现出Wannier型和电荷转移Frenkel型激子。
summaries.ja: 対称性解析とスピン分極密度汎関数理論および準粒子自己無撞着GW計算により、ウルツ鉱型構造に基づくMnSiN2とMnGeN2が交替磁性体であり、最低エネルギー磁気配置Pna'2_1'が中性子回折データと一致することが示され、交替磁性的バンド分裂、スピン波とカイラルマグノン、ネール温度の推定、およびBethe-Salpeter法による光学誘電関数が報告され、MnSiN2はWannier型励起子と電荷移動Frenkel型励起子の両方を示す。

title: Generalized dielectric-dependent hybrid functional combining Gaussian and Yukawa screening
abstract: We develop a generalized Coulomb-attenuated method (GCAM) for dielectric-dependent hybrid functionals that combines Gaussian and Yukawa-type screening functions to provide an accurate representation of the random-phase approximation (RPA) dielectric function. Through systematic fitting to RPA dielectric functions of semiconductors and insulators, and to the Lindhard dielectric function of the homogeneous electron gas, we demonstrate that GCAM significantly reduces errors in the model dielectric function across the full momentum range. However, despite this improved physical description of screening, band gap calculations reveal that GCAM yields larger errors compared to experiment than previous CAM approaches for wide-gap materials, but smaller errors for most narrow-gap materials. This counterintuitive result demonstrates that the success of CAM stems not purely from physical reasons, but also from a partial cancellation of errors. In contrast, for optical absorption spectra calculated within a model Bethe-Salpeter equation framework, GCAM systematically outperforms CAM, showing better agreement with the reference spectra obtained with the diagonal RPA screening in both peak positions and relative intensities. Our findings reveal the important role of error cancellation in dielectric-dependent hybrid functionals.

summaries.en: The generalized Coulomb-attenuated method (GCAM) combines Gaussian and Yukawa screening to model RPA dielectric functions more accurately across momentum space, but while it improves optical absorption spectra, it yields larger band-gap errors for wide-gap materials and smaller errors for most narrow-gap materials, revealing that error cancellation plays an important role in dielectric-dependent hybrid functionals.
summaries.zh: 广义库仑衰减方法（GCAM）结合高斯和汤川屏蔽以在全动量范围内更准确地模拟RPA介电函数，虽然它改善了光学吸收谱，但对宽禁带材料的带隙误差更大、对大多数窄禁带材料误差更小，表明误差抵消在介电依赖杂化泛函中起重要作用。
summaries.ja: 一般化クーロン減衰法（GCAM）はガウス型と湯川型の遮蔽を組み合わせて全運動量範囲でRPA誘電関数をより正確に表現するが、光学吸収スペクトルは改善する一方で、ワイドギャップ材料ではバンドギャップ誤差が大きくナロウギャップ材料の多くでは小さくなり、誤差の相殺が誘電依存ハイブリッド汎関数において重要な役割を果たすことを示している。

title: HEP-like 1550 nm wide-field pixelated optical receiver for inter-satellite laser links: a simulation-based proof of concept for Earth, lunar and Earth-Moon scenarios
abstract: I propose and evaluate by simulation a wide-field dome optical receiver (a field of view larger than a hemisphere) at 1550 nm for the acquisition of inter-satellite laser links. The detector is an InGaAs pixel hybrid of about 1 Mpixel with event-driven, time-stamped readout, inspired by the pixel detectors of high-energy physics. A pulsed beacon is detected by the coincidence of m hits in a sliding block of pixels, and the angle of arrival (AoA) is estimated by clustering and centroiding and handed to a narrow-field data channel. In a 550 km Earth constellation, with a 5 mrad beacon and a 10 mm aperture, detection takes 12 $\mu$s to 2 ms (up to 116 ms with the 6-9 mm that the optics allow), with a whole-frame false-alarm rate below 0.01/s, and the AoA error is 0.13-0.23 mrad. Cooling to about 233 K gives a service life above 5 years for fluences up to about $2\times10^{9}$ p/cm$^2$ per year. The receiver is also studied around the Moon and on the Earth-Moon link, where it works only between high orbits. Compared phase by phase with published scan-based acquisition, the search phase (3-18 ms with 10 mm) is shorter by a factor of about $10^{2}$ to $10^{5}$; end to end, with assumed pointing and loop-closure times, it takes 0.16-1.5 s, comparable to a terminal with calibrated open-loop pointing but without requiring that pointing at the receiver; the partner's beacon must still be pointed at it to about 1.25 mrad (5 mrad beacon). All values are simulation results, obtained with idealised optics and a 1 Mpixel detector that does not exist today; none is a measurement.
subjects: Instrumentation and Detectors (physics.ins-det) ; Signal Processing (eess.SP); Optics (physics.optics)

summaries.en: Simulations show that a 1550 nm wide-field InGaAs pixelated optical receiver inspired by high-energy-physics detectors can acquire inter-satellite laser links with microsecond-to-millisecond detection, sub-mrad angle-of-arrival accuracy, and a search phase roughly 10^2-10^5 times shorter than published scan-based acquisition, although all results rely on idealized optics and a 1 Mpixel detector that does not yet exist.
summaries.zh: 模拟结果表明，一种受高能物理探测器启发、工作在1550 nm的宽视场InGaAs像素化光学接收机能够捕获星间激光链路，探测时间为微秒至毫秒量级，到达角精度优于毫弧度量级，其搜索阶段比已发表的扫描式捕获快约10^2至10^5倍，但所有结果均基于理想化光学系统和尚不存在的1 Mpixel探测器。
summaries.ja: シミュレーションにより、高エネルギー物理学の検出器に着想を得た1550 nmの広視野InGaAsピクセル型光受信機が、マイクロ秒からミリ秒の検出時間とサブミリラジアンの到来角精度で衛星間レーザリンクを捕捉でき、その探索段階は既発表のスキャン方式より約10^2〜10^5倍短いことが示されたが、すべての結果は理想化された光学系と未だ存在しない1 Mpixel検出器に基づくものである。

title: In-pixel lock-in readout for wide-field nitrogen-vacancy radio-frequency spectrum analysis
abstract: The growing use of radio-frequency (RF) technologies requires compact, room-temperature sensors that can analyze a wide RF band in real time. Here we present a quantum RF spectrum analyzer based on the gradient-encoded electron spin resonance of a nitrogen-vacancy (NV) ensemble in diamond and read out with a $512\times542$-pixel lock-in camera that demodulates the signal in each pixel. On/off keying the signal under test at the camera's reference frequency lets every pixel extract the spin-resonant photoluminescence modulation. Before digitization, each pixel suppresses the static background and low-frequency noise that limit conventional camera readout. Translating a single permanent magnet tunes the encoded band continuously from 10~MHz to 32~GHz. The magnet position establishes a trade-off between instantaneous bandwidth (up to 4~GHz) and frequency resolution (7--22~MHz), with a 5~ms readout time. The wide-field readout integrates all spectral channels in parallel in a room-temperature sensor head and requires no phase synchronization to the RF carrier. The SNR remains above 70 at an applied power as low as $-32.5$~dBm. The magnetic-field configuration can be adapted to different RF bands without changing the pixel-parallel readout.

summaries.en: A 512×542-pixel lock-in camera demodulates gradient-encoded nitrogen-vacancy electron spin resonance in diamond to perform room-temperature quantum radio-frequency spectrum analysis from 10 MHz to 32 GHz with up to 4 GHz instantaneous bandwidth and 5 ms readout.
summaries.zh: 一种512×542像素的锁相相机对金刚石中梯度编码的氮空位电子自旋共振信号进行逐像素解调，实现了室温量子射频频谱分析，频率范围可从10 MHz连续调谐至32 GHz，瞬时带宽最高4 GHz，读出时间为5 ms。
summaries.ja: 512×542ピクセルのロックインカメラでダイヤモンド中の窒素空孔中心の勾配エンコードされた電子スピン共鳴を画素ごとに復調することにより、10 MHzから32 GHzまで連続同調可能で最大4 GHzの瞬時帯域幅と5 msの読み出し時間を持つ室温量子高周波スペクトラム分析が実現された。

title: Machine-learning-assisted photon pairing for neutral-pion reconstruction at future Higgs factories
abstract: Neutral-pion ($\pi^0$) reconstruction is important for precision measurements at high-energy colliders, particularly in flavor, $\tau$, and Higgs physics. We study $\pi^0$ candidate selection in four benchmark physics processes at electron--positron colliders, comparing an optimized diphoton mass-window (MW) baseline with four machine-learning methods: a boosted decision tree (BDT), a multilayer perceptron (MLP), ParticleNet (PN), and Particle Transformer (ParT). Performance is evaluated using the product of selection efficiency and purity. At the reference ECAL energy resolution, all four machine-learning methods outperform MW. PN and ParT achieve relative improvements of 53%--95% and 60%--128%, respectively, primarily through better rejection of incorrectly matched photon pairs. Their performance advantage is maintained across the investigated ECAL energy resolutions. Training-sample-size scans reveal two periods of rapid performance improvement separated by slower growth in most PN and ParT learning curves. The improved candidate selection provides a starting point for further studies of $\rho$ and hadronic $\tau$ reconstruction.
subjects: Instrumentation and Detectors (physics.ins-det) ; High Energy Physics - Experiment (hep-ex)

summaries.en: This study shows that machine-learning methods, particularly ParticleNet and Particle Transformer, substantially outperform a diphoton mass-window baseline for neutral-pion candidate selection at future electron-positron Higgs factories, mainly by rejecting incorrectly matched photon pairs, with advantages robust across ECAL energy resolutions.
summaries.zh: 本研究表明，在未来的正负电子希格斯工厂中，机器学习方法（尤其是ParticleNet和Particle Transformer）通过更好地排除错误配对的 photon 对，在中性π介子候选者选择上显著优于双光子质量窗基线方法，且其优势在不同ECAL能量分辨率下均保持稳定。
summaries.ja: 本研究は、将来の電子-陽電子ヒッグス工場において、機械学習手法、特にParticleNetとParticle Transformerが、誤って対にされた光子対の排除を改善することで、二光子質量ウィンドウのベースラインを大きく上回る中性パイ中間子候補選択性能を示し、その優位性がECALエネルギー分解能によらず維持されることを明らかにした。

title: Organ-scale pulsatile blood flow reconstruction in the avian yolk sac embryo
abstract: The hemodynamic forces on endothelial cells in developing vascular networks vary over the cardiac cycle. Resolving these variations throughout the yolk sac requires imaging individual regions of the vasculature at different times. We reconstructed mean and pulsatile blood flow in a 21-somite quail embryo from 53 overlapping high-speed microscopy recordings acquired over 3.7 h. We reconciled mean-flow measurements using conservation of flux at vascular junctions and synchronized cardiac phases using vessels shared between recordings. Of the 7,009 vessels with flow measurements in the computational domain, we reconstructed pulsatile flow in 5,214. Relative pulsatility decreased along an arterial-side path but increased along a venous-return path, where downstream flow oscillations preceded those upstream. Across the plexus, phase lags relative to the vitelline veins increased toward the vascular margin. A distributed resistance--compliance model with uniform vessel distensibility reproduced many of these spatial variations. Our results suggest that vascular geometry and compliance, together with pulsatile forcing from both arterial and venous boundaries, determine the local flow waveforms within the developing plexus.

summaries.en: By combining 53 overlapping high-speed microscopy recordings of a quail yolk sac embryo, the authors reconstructed pulsatile blood flow in 5,214 of 7,009 measured vessels and showed that a distributed resistance-compliance model with uniform vessel distensibility reproduces many of the observed spatial variations in flow waveform.
summaries.zh: 作者通过整合鹌鹑卵黄囊胚胎的53段重叠高速显微成像记录，在7,009条测得血流的血管中重建了5,214条的搏动性血流，并表明一个具有均匀血管扩张性的分布式阻力-顺应性模型能够重现所观察到的许多血流波形空间变化。
summaries.ja: 著者らはウズラ卵黄嚢胚の53の重複する高速顕微鏡記録を統合し、血流が測定された7,009本の血管のうち5,214本で拍動性血流を再構築し、均一な血管拡張性を持つ分布型抵抗-コンプライアンスモデルが観察された血流波形の空間的変化の多くを再現できることを示した。

title: Observation of collective flatbands in hybrid Mie-grating THz metasurfaces
abstract: We propose a novel type of functional metasurfaces created by a hybridization of Mie resonators with high-index optical gratings. We demonstrate that such hybrid metasurfaces possess flatbands characterized by zero group velocity and strong energy localization. We experimentally observe the flatbands in free-standing terahertz (THz) metasurfaces, where dielectric interconnections between Mie resonators, forming the grating, mediate multipolar hybridization and provide a geometric control over collective resonances. Our THz near-field measurements with a dipole excitation uncover long-lived coherent oscillations associated with the quasi-flat magnetic-dipolar resonant modes, while a spatial mapping resolves the resonant electromagnetic response across the dielectric interconnections. We vary the grating width continuously to tune the hybrid magnetic-dipolar resonances and substantially enhance the quality factor (Q factor), while preserving the quasi-!atband dispersion. Complementary Bloch-resolved Purcell calculations reveal the substantial Purcell enhancement with increasing Q factor, followed by a trend towards saturation and highlighting the interplay between radiative confinement and local emitter-mode coupling. We believe our findings establish the engineering of dielectric interconnections in periodic lattices as a novel strategy for spectrally tuning high-Q flatbands in these metastructures, tailoring localized electromagnetic interactions in functional optical metasurfaces.

summaries.en: The paper experimentally demonstrates collective flatbands with zero group velocity and strong energy localization in hybrid Mie-grating terahertz metasurfaces, where dielectric interconnections between Mie resonators mediate multipolar hybridization and allow geometric tuning of high-quality-factor quasi-flat magnetic-dipolar resonances.
summaries.zh: 该论文在混合Mie光栅太赫兹超表面中实验观测到具有零群速度和强能量局域化的集体平带，其中Mie谐振器之间的介电互连介导多极杂化，并可通过几何调控实现高品质因子的准平坦磁偶极共振。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、Mie共振器間の誘電体相互接続が多極ハイブリダイゼーションを媒介し、高品質因子の準フラットな磁気双極子共鳴を幾何学的に制御できるハイブリッドMieグレーティングテラヘルツメタサーフェスにおいて、ゼロ群速度と強いエネルギー局在を持つ集団フラットバンドを実験的に観測した。

title: Picojoule-level self-referencing with dual dispersive waves in thin-film lithium niobate
abstract: We demonstrate pulse-energy-efficient f-2f self-referencing of telecom-band pulses in a monolithic thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) waveguide that combines Kerr spectral broadening with quasi-phase-matched (QPM) second-harmonic generation (SHG). Dispersion engineering generates dual dispersive waves (DWs) near 1 and 2 um, placed symmetrically around the pump to reduce the required spectral broadening. With an on-chip pulse energy of only 16.8 pJ, we detect a carrier-envelope-offset frequency (fceo) beatnote with a 32 dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and we stabilize the fceo of an Er-fiber laser at 30 pJ, which is, to our knowledge, the lowest pulse energy reported for fceo stabilization at telecom wavelengths. Compared with an identical waveguide without poling, the QPM section enhances the beatnote SNR by 43 dB and reduces the required pulse energy fourfold. We further show that a mode-crossing DW, a chirped poling period, and a poled section aligned with the onset of DW generation to mitigate temporal walk-off are key to this performance.

summaries.en: Pulse-energy-efficient f-2f self-referencing is demonstrated in a monolithic thin-film lithium niobate waveguide that combines Kerr spectral broadening with quasi-phase-matched second-harmonic generation, where dispersion-engineered dual dispersive waves near 1 and 2 µm reduce the required broadening and enable a carrier-envelope-offset beatnote at 32 dB SNR with only 16.
summaries.zh: 本文在单片薄膜铌酸锂波导中演示了脉冲能量高效的f-2f自参考，该波导将克尔光谱展宽与准相位匹配二次谐波产生相结合，通过色散工程在1微米和2微米附近产生对称分布于泵浦两侧的双色散波以降低所需展宽，在仅16.

title: Cryogenic Luminescence Thermometry of Upconversion Micro- and Nanoparticles via Deep Learning
abstract: Luminescence thermometry with single or optically trapped particles is hampered by weak signals that fluctuate with alignment, collection efficiency, and excitation conditions and, for $\mathrm{Er}^{3+}$-based probes, by the loss of sensitivity of the luminescence intensity ratio (LIR) at cryogenic temperatures. Here we use a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) to predict the temperature directly from single emission spectra of $\mathrm{NaYF}_4{:}\mathrm{Yb}^{3+},\mathrm{Er}^{3+}$ micro- and nanoparticles between $-150\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and $105\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, and compare it with the standard LIR under adverse conditions deliberately reproduced with particle ensembles. From $-150\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $30\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, the 1D-CNN reduces the single-spectrum mean absolute error from $5.4\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $1.0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and keeps its temperature uncertainty nearly constant down to the lowest temperatures, where Stark-component features remain temperature dependent while the LIR loses its sensitivity. Under deliberate optical misalignment, its error increases only from $0.58\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $0.88\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, whereas that of the LIR rises from $1.4\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $3.5\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The same approach reaches sub-degree accuracy ($0.21\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$) over a narrow temperature window and a single calibration valid across different pump powers and wavelengths. These results establish 1D-CNNs as robust single-shot thermometers and a step toward fast thermometry of single and trapped particles.

summaries.en: A one-dimensional convolutional neural network applied to single emission spectra of NaYF4:Yb3+,Er3+ micro- and nanoparticles enables robust cryogenic luminescence thermometry, reducing the single-spectrum mean absolute error from 5.

title: Inverse design of polarization-analyzing gratings
abstract: Metasurface polarization analyzing gratings have attracted increasing interest for polarization management and sensing in optical systems. Traditional strategies for the design of these gratings are based on a formalism combining the Jones calculus with Fourier optics. While this approach has achieved notable success in numerous applications, its validity is restricted to the paraxial regime. Here we introduce a differentiable topology optimization framework for these gratings which is free of this constraint. We show that this framework can yield designs which outperform the traditional approach, especially at high angles. Additionally, we provide preliminary experimental validation to corroborate these results.

summaries.en: A differentiable topology optimization framework enables inverse design of metasurface polarization-analyzing gratings beyond the paraxial regime, outperforming traditional Jones-calculus and Fourier-optics designs, especially at high angles, with preliminary experimental validation.
summaries.zh: 一种可微拓扑优化框架实现了超越傍轴近似限制的超表面偏振分析光栅逆向设计，其性能优于传统的琼斯计算与傅里叶光学方法，尤其在大角度下更为显著，并获得了初步实验验证。
summaries.ja: 微分可能なトポロジー最適化フレームワークにより、近軸近似の制約を超えたメタサーフェス偏光解析グレーティングの逆設計が可能となり、従来のジョーンズ計算とフーリエ光学に基づく設計を特に高角度で上回る性能を示し、予備的な実験検証も行われた。

title: Excited-state lifetime and decay mechanisms in erbium-doped ZBLAN using Variable Excited-State dual-Pump Analysis
abstract: This work presents a new technique for measuring excited-state lifetimes of rare-earth ions. This technique is particularly powerful for states that are very short lived or have a low photon yield because their de-excitation pathways are dominated by non-radiative processes. The technique uses dual optical parametric oscillators, whose pulses are separated by a variable delay. It reconstructs the excited-state decay curve from a series of delayed fluorescence intensity spectra rather than directly recording the fluorescence decay as done in conventional time-resolved laser fluorescence spectroscopy. The power of the technique is demonstrated by measuring the lifetime of the short-lived $^4I_{9/2}$ level in Er$^{3+}$-doped ZBLAN, which is well-known for its low photon yield. The technique enables accurate measurement of its lifetime and suggests a new depopulating mechanism involving the $^4I_{9/2}$ level in ZBLAN glass. Its accuracy is validated by measuring the lifetime of the $^4F_{9/2}$ state achieving excellent agreement with conventional time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy measurements. The approach is well suited for measuring lifetimes ranging from the sub-microsecond to the millisecond range. It provides a versatile platform for investigating excited-state dynamics and energy-transfer processes in RE-doped materials.

summaries.en: The paper introduces a variable excited-state dual-pump technique using two delayed optical parametric oscillator pulses to reconstruct excited-state decay curves from delayed fluorescence spectra, enabling accurate lifetime measurement of the short-lived, low-photon-yield 4I9/2 level in Er3+-doped ZBLAN and revealing a new depopulating mechanism while being validated on the 4F9/2 state.
summaries.zh: 该论文提出了一种可变激发态双泵浦技术，利用两束具有可变延迟的光学参量振荡器脉冲，从一系列延迟荧光光谱重建激发态衰减曲线，从而精确测量了Er3+掺杂ZBLAN中寿命短、光子产率低的4I9/2能级寿命，揭示了新的去布居机制，并通过4F9/2能级的测量验证了该方法的准确性。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、可変遅延を持つ2つの光パラメトリック発振器パルスを用いて遅延蛍光スペクトルから励起状態の減衰曲線を再構成する可変励起状態デュアルポンプ法を提案し、Er3+添加ZBLANにおける短寿命で光子収率の低い4I9/2準位の寿命を正確に測定するとともに新たな無輻射失活機構を示唆し、4F9/2準位の測定によりその精度を検証した。

title: MCP-based EUV ptychography with physics-simulation-trained residual learning
abstract: Microchannel-plate (MCP) detectors offer high gain for extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) experiments, but spatial blur and nonlinear response hinder quantitative diffraction imaging. Here, we present an MCP-based EUV ptychography system that combines detector hardware with physics-simulation-trained computational restoration. A residual-learning neural network trained on simulated detector degradation restores diffraction patterns without experimentally acquired training pairs. This preprocessing substantially improves image quality compared with reconstructions from uncorrected data under identical reconstruction settings. Single-harmonic imaging at $57$~nm yields an effective edge-response width of $1.08~\mu$m, approaching the nominal diffraction-limited scale of the imaging geometry. The approach further enables wavelength-multiplexed imaging at $44.4$ and $57$~nm. By coupling high-gain detection with computational compensation, this system enables high-resolution, multi-harmonic EUV ptychography and offers a cost-effective alternative to scientific-grade EUV CCD detectors

summaries.en: An MCP-based EUV ptychography system uses a residual-learning neural network trained on simulated detector degradation to correct diffraction patterns without experimental training pairs, achieving an effective edge-response width of 1.
summaries.zh: 基于MCP的极紫外叠层成像系统采用在模拟探测器退化数据上训练的残差学习神经网络，无需实验配对的训练数据即可校正衍射图样，在57 nm波长下实现1.

title: Multiscale wave-coupled neural networks for the inverse-design of broadband diffractive optics
abstract: In this work, we introduce an inverse-design model called multiscale wave-coupled neural networks (MSWNets) inspired by physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) that integrate the deep-learning capability of fully-connected neural networks with rigorous Rayleigh-Sommerfeld diffraction theory. MSWNets are trained using spatial input and output functions describing the height profiles of diffractive structures. Importantly, a MSWNet is composed of multiple sub-networks that provide learning across multiple frequency components of the optimal design solution. First, we validate and analyze the inverse design capabilities of the MSWNets' architecture through training on the complete complex field propagated from the analytical design of an axilens, demonstrating accurate reconstruction. Finally, we employ MSWNets, trained to maximize focusing efficiency, for the inverse design of novel diffractive devices. In particular, we design and display the performance of several achromatic lenses and doublets across the mid-wave infrared region ($3-5\rm{\;\mu} m$) with focal distance $f=500\rm{\;\mu m}$, demonstrating the potential of our inverse-design framework for the next-generation of broadband diffractive optical devices.

summaries.en: The paper introduces multiscale wave-coupled neural networks (MSWNets), a physics-informed inverse-design framework combining fully connected neural networks with Rayleigh-Sommerfeld diffraction theory, and demonstrates its use in designing broadband diffractive optics such as achromatic lenses and doublets in the mid-wave infrared region.
summaries.zh: 本文提出了多尺度波耦合神经网络（MSWNets），这是一种受物理信息神经网络启发、将全连接神经网络与严格瑞利-索末菲衍射理论相结合的逆向设计框架，并展示了其在中波红外波段设计消色差透镜和双合透镜等宽带衍射光学器件中的应用。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、全結合ニューラルネットワークと厳密なレイリー・ゾンマーフェルト回折理論を統合した物理情報ニューラルネットワークに着想を得た逆設計フレームワークであるマルチスケール波結合ニューラルネットワーク（MSWNets）を提案し、中波赤外域におけるアクロマティックレンズやダブレットなどの広帯域回折光学素子の設計への応用を示す。

title: Parallel Two-Photon Lithography: From Optical Nonlinearities to Energy Limits, Dose Control and Throughput Benchmarks
abstract: Two-photon lithography (TPL) prints three-dimensional polymer architectures with sub-diffraction features, but writing them voxel by voxel limits its throughput. This review examines how parallelization overcomes this limit with fixed multi-focus arrays, reconfigurable holography using spatial light modulators and digital micromirror devices, hybrid metalens arrays, shaped beams, temporally focused projection and two-step absorption. An energy-deposition framework built on measured nonlinear absorption coefficients shows how the absorption order and coefficients of a resist determine its voxel size, energy per voxel and attainable voxel rate. Applied to parallel writing, the framework quantifies the costs of non-uniform foci, coherent crosstalk between foci, side-lobe losses in shaped beams and weaker axial confinement in projection. Published systems reach peak rates above $10^{8}$ voxels s$^{-1}$ with scanned focus arrays and up to $1.7\times10^{9}$ voxels s$^{-1}$ with grayscale projection under a fine-voxel definition, and parallel features as small as 20-55 nm. As rates rise, however, dose uniformity, proximity effects, heat, stitching and data bandwidth increasingly limit fidelity. A minimum reporting standard that includes the energy per voxel and sustained part-level rates is therefore proposed, together with priorities for the field: shared benchmark parts, predictive dose control and resists designed for parallel writing.

summaries.en: Two-photon lithography (TPL) prints three-dimensional polymer architectures with sub-diffraction features, but writing them voxel by voxel limits its throughput.

title: Efficient phase-only wavefront shaping at 250 kHz for multimode fiber endomicroscopy
abstract: Wavefront shaping through multimode fibers (MMFs) enables diffraction-limited fluorescence imaging with hair-thin probes, at a speed and light budget bounded by the wavefront modulator. Existing modulators provide at most two of three key characteristics: high refresh rate, (high) modal dimensionality, and light efficiency. Here, we demonstrate wavefront control through an MMF using a tailored phase-only microelectromechanical modulator that combines all three, with 8,192 elements arranged in a 32 x 256 array, 7-bit phase control, and a 250 kHz full-frame refresh rate. Direct on-axis phase modulation delivers 70+/-5% of the incident light into the modulated field and eliminates both off-axis encoding optical losses and hologram computation. The generated foci at the distal end of the fiber remain isotropic with high fidelity. We use singular-value decomposition analysis of the measured transmission to identify the effective degrees of freedom of our system. By scanning the focus at multiple depths, we demonstrate volumetric fluorescence imaging. These results open a new operating regime for adaptive in vivo multimode-fiber endoscopy.

summaries.en: A tailored phase-only microelectromechanical modulator with 8,192 elements and a 250 kHz full-frame refresh rate enables high-efficiency, high-dimensionality wavefront shaping through multimode fibers for volumetric fluorescence endomicroscopy.

title: Optical Motion Sensing for Piezoelectric-Resonator-Based Power Converters
abstract: Piezoelectric components present a promising alternative to conventional magnetics for miniaturized, high-frequency power converters. While high-Q piezoelectric resonators have demonstrated high efficiencies and large power densities in prototype high-frequency dc-dc converters, their optimal operating conditions are sensitive to temperature fluctuations and load variations. Therefore, robust closed-loop control is essential for practical deployment. Electrical approaches for sensing motional current may compromise the electrical isolation and electromagnetic interference (EMI) immunity inherently provided by the mechanical nature of these resonators. Here, we present an optical motion sensing approach for piezoelectric power converters. The optical sensing system comprises a laser, fiber optics, and a photodetector. The proposed approach uses optical interference to monitor the mechanical displacement in real time. The resulting optical signal carries both the amplitude and phase of the mechanical motion, which are necessary for closed-loop control. We experimentally characterize and validate this optical motion sensing approach using a 45-kHz piezoelectric resonator driven by a GaN half bridge with input voltages up to 45 V. We further experimentally demonstrate closed-loop control using the proposed optical motion sensing for a 99-kHz isolated piezoelectric converter. These initial results establish a viable pathway toward optically closed-loop control of piezoelectric power converters.

summaries.en: This paper presents an optical interferometry-based motion sensing approach using a laser, fiber optics, and a photodetector to monitor the mechanical displacement of piezoelectric resonators in real time, capturing both amplitude and phase for closed-loop control of piezoelectric power converters.
summaries.zh: 本文提出了一种基于激光、光纤和光电探测器的光学干涉运动传感方法，可实时监测压电谐振器的机械位移并获取其幅度与相位信息，用于压电功率变换器的闭环控制。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、レーザー、光ファイバー、フォトディテクタを用いた光干渉による運動センシング手法を提案し、圧電共振器の機械的変位をリアルタイムで監視して振幅と位相の両方を取得し、圧電電力変換器の閉ループ制御を可能にする。

title: Uniguided and unicoupled resonances in an asymmetric acoustic metasurface
abstract: We theoretically study an acoustic metasurface that exhibits ultimate asymmetry in absorption under oblique incidence. This behavior arises from a counter-propagating pair of uniguided (UGR) and unicoupled (UCR) resonances. The UGR radiates to only one side, while the UCR radiates to both sides but can be excited from only one. In the lossless regime, the transmission phase winds by $2\pi$ across both UCR and UGR while the transmittance remains flat at any prescribed nonzero level. Thermoviscous losses introduce resonant intensity modulation and enable critical coupling, yielding perfect sound absorption exclusively for incidence through the channel that excites the UCR. Therefore, asymmetric metasurfaces with UCR and UGR offer a route to full phase control and perfect sound absorption.

summaries.en: This theoretical study shows that an asymmetric acoustic metasurface supporting counter-propagating uniguided (UGR) and unicoupled (UCR) resonances achieves complete phase control with flat transmittance in the lossless regime and, with thermoviscous losses, perfect sound absorption exclusively for incidence through the channel that excites the UCR.
summaries.zh: 这项理论研究证明，支持反向传播的单导（UGR）与单耦（UCR）共振的非对称声学超表面在无损耗情形下可实现透射率保持恒定而相位绕转2π的完全相位调控，并在引入热黏性损耗后仅对经激发UCR通道入射的声波实现完美吸声。
summaries.ja: この理論研究は、逆方向に伝搬する単ガイド（UGR）共鳴と単結合（UCR）共鳴を有する非対称音響メタサーフェスが、無損失領域では透過率を一定に保ちながら2πの位相制御を実現し、熱粘性損失の導入によりUCRを励起する側からの入射に対してのみ完全吸音を達成することを示した。

title: Acoustic bound states in the continuum in a labyrinthine meta-atom
abstract: In this Letter, we theoretically and experimentally study acoustic bound states in the continuum (BICs) emerging in labyrinth meta-atom embedded in an acoustic waveguide. A symmetry-protected BIC is supported in the lossless limit when the meta-atom is positioned on the waveguide axis. Breaking the symmetry by shifting the meta-atom away from the center of the waveguide transforms the BIC into a radiative quasi-BIC, manifested by the emergence of a narrow resonant feature in the transmittance spectrum. The proposed concept is experimentally tested using a 3D-printed labyrinthine meta-atom placed inside an impedance tube. The measured transmittance spectra are consistent with numerical simulations and support the BIC-to-quasi-BIC transition induced by symmetry breaking in the presence of thermoviscous losses. The resonance frequency, contrast, and linewidth can be controlled by varying the meta-atom position. The observed behavior is interpreted within a two-mode temporal coupled-mode theory (TCMT), providing an analytical description of the resonant response. The ability to tune radiative leakage in the presence of absorption makes the proposed acoustic BIC platform promising for the development of tunable absorbers, sensors, and modulators.

summaries.en: This Letter theoretically and experimentally demonstrates symmetry-protected acoustic bound states in the continuum (BICs) in a labyrinthine meta-atom embedded in a waveguide, where shifting the meta-atom off-axis breaks symmetry to convert the BIC into a radiative quasi-BIC with a narrow transmittance resonance whose frequency, contrast, and linewidth are tunable and described by two-mode temporal coupled-mode theory.
summaries.zh: 本文从理论和实验上研究了嵌入声波导中的迷宫式超原子所支持的声学连续域束缚态（BIC），当超原子偏离波导轴线破坏对称性时，对称保护BIC转变为辐射性准BIC并在透射谱中表现为窄共振，其频率、对比度和线宽可通过改变超原子位置调控，并用双模时间耦合模理论予以解释。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、音響導波路内に埋め込まれた迷路型メタ原子における対称性保護された音響連続域束縛状態（BIC）を理論的・実験的に示し、メタ原子を導波路軸からずらして対称性を破ることでBICが放射準BICへと転換され透過スペクトルに狭い共鳴が現れ、その周波数・コントラスト・線幅が位置により制御可能で二モード時間結合モード理論で記述されることを明らかにした。

title: Reconfigurable Microwave Photonic All-Pass Filters based on Optical Kerr Microcombs
abstract: Microwave photonic (MWP) all pass filters (APFs), which enable phase manipulation without altering signal amplitudes, are essential for phase engineering in high bandwidth microwave signal processing. However, achieving a high degree of reconfigurability in the filter order and characteristic parameters of APFs remains challenging for conventional methods. Here, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a new strategy for realizing MWP APFs based on a microcomb driven transversal filter system, enabling high reconfigurability, sharp phase transitions with high group delays, and low loss. We experimentally demonstrate both 1st and 2nd order APFs, achieving a maximum amplitude variation (MAV) of 1.95 dB and a maximum group delay (MGD) of 580 ps for the former, and a MAV of 2.01 dB and an MGD of 1740 ps for the latter. In addition, both independent and joint tuning of APF characteristic parameters are demonstrated by simply programming the tap coefficients without changing any hardware, enabling highly reconfigurable filter response for diverse phase engineering functionalities. These results highlight the potential of our approach for implementing MWP APFs with both high performance and reconfigurability for practical applications requiring dynamic and versatile phase control.

summaries.en: The paper proposes and experimentally demonstrates reconfigurable microwave photonic all-pass filters based on a microcomb-driven transversal filter system, achieving first- and second-order filters with maximum group delays of 580 ps and 1740 ps and maximum amplitude variations of 1.
summaries.zh: 该论文提出并实验演示了一种基于微梳驱动的横向滤波系统的可重构微波光子全通滤波器，实现了最大群延迟分别为580 ps和1740 ps、最大幅度变化分别为1.
summaries.ja: 本論文は、マイクロコム駆動型トランスバーサルフィルタシステムに基づく再構成可能なマイクロ波フォトニック全通過フィルタを提案・実証し、最大群遅延580 psおよび1740 ps、最大振幅変動1.

title: A Camera-Based Single-Volume, Monolithic Compton Camera
abstract: A Compton camera measures two events in a detector from individual gamma-rays to reconstruct the radiation source. Conventional scintillator-based Compton cameras consist of two separate scintillator volumes or a single segmented scintillator, resulting in drawbacks regarding detector bulkiness and efficiency. Their scintillator readout techniques struggle to resolve two nearby events in one monolithic scintillator. Single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) cameras have recently been proposed for measuring scintillation events in various configurations. SPAD array sensors enable high-resolution photon-counting acquisition at high rates that is easily scalable to millions of pixels. Prior work has explored different optics and measurement arrangements as well as demonstrated measurement of single interaction locations. In this work, we extend these capabilities to demonstrate a practical radiation imaging device in the form of a Compton camera consisting of a SPAD camera and one compact, monolithic scintillator. Our Compton camera prototype successfully reconstructs a gamma-ray source over multiple locations that span a 4$\pi$ steradian field of view. Our approach is able to resolve two simultaneous events in one monolithic scintillator and enables Compton camera devices with compact, monolithic scintillator volumes for enhanced portability.
subjects: Instrumentation and Detectors (physics.ins-det) ; Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Image and Video Processing (eess.IV)

summaries.en: This work demonstrates a practical Compton camera that uses a single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) camera coupled to one compact monolithic scintillator to resolve two simultaneous scintillation events and reconstruct gamma-ray sources across a 4π steradian field of view.
summaries.zh: 本工作展示了一种实用的康普顿相机，它利用单光子雪崩二极管（SPAD）相机与单个紧凑的整体闪烁体耦合，能够分辨两个同时发生的闪烁事件，并在4π球面度视场内重建伽马射线源。
summaries.ja: 本研究は、単一光子アバランシェダイオード（SPAD）カメラと1つのコンパクトなモノリシックシンチレータを組み合わせた実用的なコンプトンカメラを実証し、同時に生じる2つのシンチレーション事象を識別して4πステラジアンの視野にわたるガンマ線源を再構成する。

title: 2D MXene integrated optical polarizers based on TiO2 with high performance
abstract: Polarization control is essential for modern optical systems. Recently, two dimensional (2D) materials featuring highly anisotropic absorption across broad wavelength regions have emerged as a promising solution for realizing optical polarizers with operation bandwidths far exceeding those achievable using bulk materials. Despite this, existing 2D material based optical polarizers face critical limitations in simultaneously delivering high polarizer figures of merit (FOMs), robust power endurance, and scalable fabrication, hindering their practical deployment beyond laboratory. Here, we overcome this bottleneck by demonstrating optical polarizers through integrating 2D MXene films onto silicon photonic devices and subsequently converting them in situ into 2D titanium dioxide (TiO2). The 2D TiO2 exhibits significantly improved anisotropic absorption and thermal / chemical stability compared with MXene, enabling the hybrid polarizers to achieve a record high polarizer FOM of 17.5 (among 2D material-coated devices) and excellent power tolerance (stable under > 2 W coupled average power), together with a broad operation bandwidth (> 140 nm) and a high fabrication yield ( 98%). We also demonstrate microring resonator polarizers achieving high polarization extinction ratios up to 12 dB. With outstanding overall performance and strong capability for large-scale manufacturing, these polarizers represent a solid step towards industry ready implementations of 2D material based optical polarizers.

summaries.en: By integrating 2D MXene films onto silicon photonic devices and converting them in situ into 2D TiO2, the authors demonstrate hybrid optical polarizers with a record figure of merit of 17.

title: Polarization-independent self-hybridized strong coupling by Brillouin zone folding induced quasi-bound states in the continuum in bulk WS2 metasurfaces
abstract: High-refractive-index dielectric metasurfaces supporting optical modes are ideal candidates for achieving strong coupling with transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) materials. However, optical illumination with a specific polarization is always required to estimate the maximal coupling strength in such coupled systems due to the polarization-dependent optical modes. Here, we propose a self-hybridized strong coupling between Brillouin zone folding induced quasi-bound states in the continuum (BZF-QBICs) mode and A excitons in the same bulk WS2 metasurface. By changing the thickness of the bulk WS2 metasurfaces, a typical anticrossing behavior with Rabi splitting of 165.9 meV is observed. Such Rabi splitting is unchanged when changing the polarization of the incident light from linearly to circularly polarizations, demonstrating the polarization-independent self-hybridized strong coupling. This work provides a novel method for realizing robust polarization-independent polaritons in bulk TMDCs metasurface and offers new insights for expanding the applications of polaritonic devices with arbitrary polarizations.

summaries.en: By exploiting Brillouin-zone-folding-induced quasi-bound states in the continuum in bulk WS2 metasurfaces, self-hybridized strong coupling with A excitons is demonstrated with a Rabi splitting of 165.

title: Giant thermal transduction via feedback-phase engineering in a thin-film lithium-niobate opto-electro-mechanical oscillator
abstract: Conventional resonant MEMS thermometry typically relies on the intrinsic temperature coefficient of frequency (TCF) of mechanical resonances. Here we show that embedding a suspended thin-film lithium-niobate mechanical resonator in an opto-electro-mechanical (OEM) feedback loop enhances the intrinsic coefficient by two orders of magnitude. By using laser--cavity detuning to control the loop's round-trip phase, and thus the Barkhausen-selected oscillation frequency, we engineer an effective TCF of $+1.24\times10^{4}$~ppm/K: a 100-fold enhancement and a sign reversal relative to its intrinsic TCF of $-124$~ppm/K. Temperature-dependent and open-loop phase measurements confirm that this giant response originates from feedback phase selection rather than from the passive resonator itself. This interpretation is further supported by the independently measured closed-loop oscillation frequencies and a detuning-dependent delay model. The same architecture also supports 2:1 subharmonic injection locking, yielding sub-6~Hz linewidths, reference-limited frequency stability, and tunable operation from $76.71$ to $76.82$~MHz. These results establish feedback-phase engineering as a general, post-fabrication route to both giant thermal transduction and low-noise yet tunable mechanical oscillation.

summaries.en: Embedding a suspended thin-film lithium-niobate mechanical resonator in an opto-electro-mechanical feedback loop and using laser-cavity detuning to control the round-trip phase yields an effective temperature coefficient of frequency of +1.

title: Ultrabroadband, high-sensitivity time-resolved terahertz spectroscopy enabled by a Yb-based laser system
abstract: Ultrafast optical fields have introduced numerous novel light-induced states in quantum materials. Identifying these states and elucidating their formation mechanisms require comprehensive, quantitative access to nonequilibrium electrodynamics across relevant energy scales. Here, we develop a Yb-laser-based time-resolved terahertz spectroscopy (TRTS) platform combining multi-pass-cell pulse compression, spintronic terahertz generation, and air-biased coherent detection. A single time-domain waveform scan provides continuous phase-resolved spectral coverage to 25 THz ($\sim$100 meV) with a Fourier resolution of 0.1 THz ($\sim$0.4 meV). This capability enables the characterization of both low-frequency charge dynamics and higher-energy resonant excitations in quantum materials under a common temporal reference. The system achieves a single-scan time-domain signal-to-noise ratio of 72 dB with long-term waveform stability, while preserving most of the laser pulse energy for tunable excitation. Measurements on intrinsic GaAs resolve extremely weak phonon features above 23 THz and demonstrate quantitative retrieval of equilibrium and transient complex optical properties. The resulting platform can provide a more complete microscopic picture of light-induced states in quantum materials.

title: Turbulence Strength Estimation from Multiplexed Orbital Angular Momentum Beams Using Multimode Fibre Speckle
abstract: The strength of atmospheric turbulence governs how much the modes of a free-space optical link mix together. It is usually measured with a separate instrument or with a Gaussian probe beam, neither of which uses the beams that a structured-light link already carries. Here we show that the turbulence strength, expressed as the Fried parameter, can be estimated directly from multiplexed orbital angular momentum (OAM) beams without knowing which modes are present. The beams pass through a passive multimode fibre that turns them into speckle on a camera, and a trained weighted sum of the camera pixels (known as an extreme learning machine), averaged over a few tens of frames, gives the Fried parameter. In the laboratory with emulated turbulence, superpositions of up to eleven OAM modes give an estimate as accurate as that from a Gaussian probe beam sent through the same fibre. In all but weak turbulence the estimate is also more accurate than an ideal Strehl meter or an ideal tip/tilt sensor, providing an efficient way to estimate turbulence strength in mode-division multiplexed systems.

summaries.en: Multiplexed orbital angular momentum beams passed through a passive multimode fibre produce camera speckle whose extreme-learning-machine-weighted pixel sum, averaged over a few tens of frames, estimates the Fried parameter as accurately as a Gaussian probe beam and more accurately than ideal Strehl or tip/tilt sensors except in weak turbulence.

title: Polarization-cloaked spatiotemporal topological knots
abstract: Spatiotemporally localized topological knots encode global connectivity within a moving space-time optical wavepacket, circumventing the requirement for spatial-only eigenmodes that extend throughout three-dimensional space-filling. In conventional modalities, this connectivity is identified directly from a scalar complex field. However, knotting optical knots with the polarization state of light proves difficult to realize for ultrafast localized wavepackets. In this work, we combine oppositely wound toroidal vortex modes with orthogonal circular polarization states on the higher-order Poincaré sphere to construct vectorial electromagnetic spatiotemporal wavepackets, in which the topological connectivity is encoded in the relative phase between the polarization components. Stokes analysis shows that S_0 retains a common toroidal envelope, whereas the phase sensitive Stokes parameters S_1 and S_2 reveal winding-dependent linked and knotted trajectories; numerical simulations verify their closure, and time-sliced off-axis interferometry experimentally reconstructs the corresponding three-dimensional S_2 textures. This separation of topological connectivity from the scalar intensity envelope extends the control of spatiotemporal topology to the polarization degree of freedom and provides a versatile framework for controlling how topological information is accessed in multidimensional structured light.

summaries.en: By combining oppositely wound toroidal vortex modes with orthogonal circular polarization states on the higher-order Poincaré sphere, the authors construct vectorial spatiotemporal optical wavepackets whose topological knotting is encoded in the relative phase between polarization components and revealed through the phase-sensitive Stokes parameters S1 and S2, verified numerically and experimentally via time-sliced off-axis interferometry.

title: Experimental study of the Reynolds number effect on the mean flow and coherent structures in a 180-degree bent pipe flow using PIV
abstract: In this work, we study the effect of Reynolds number on the flow in a 180° pipe bend with a curvature of {\gamma} = 0.2. We perform planar particle image velocimetry (PIV) in the symmetry plane of the pipe for bulk Reynolds numbers ReD from 10 000 to 60 000 with water as the working fluid. To remove the refraction at the pipe wall, a hybrid method is employed. A mixture of water, glycerol and sodium iodide is used to match the refractive index of the pipe at its outer interface. The refraction at the inner interface is corrected using reverse ray tracing. The measurements are validated against direct numerical simulations at ReD = 10 000 and 20 000 and against hot-wire data from the literature at 60 000. As the Reynolds number increases, the mean velocity profiles in and downstream of the bend become flatter. Furthermore, a second vortex pair, with the opposite direction of rotation to the Dean vortices, forms further downstream, between bend angles of 116° and 126°. A modal decomposition of the planar velocity fields shows that the coherent structures keep their spatial features at all Reynolds numbers. Their Strouhal numbers remain nearly unchanged and show no monotonic trend.
